trust_decision.summary: Whether a project-owner-supplied webhook/Slack URL may be used as an outbound HTTP destination (must be public http/https, not loopback/private/link-local/metadata, revalidated on redirects and pinned against DNS rebinding); decided at notification form clean time and in the Try sender in web/, nowhere in the scheduler that actually delivers notifications.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'SSRF in notifications'; the Try button's _http_post_json does a raw urlopen to the user URL and shows the response body back on the form page (web/projects/templates/projects/notifications/save.html:115-117), so it is the obvious reproduction path.

fix_sites.module_kind: handler helper (outbound HTTP sender for Try)

fix_sites.entry_point: new shared module web/opencve/utils/ssrf.py (validate_public_http_url, safe_request) reached by the three sites above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published fix touches only web/ (forms, Try sender, new util). The real delivery path is a second implementation in scheduler/ that the fix did NOT touch; recorded as O8 instead.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The URL is now validated in the form before it is saved, so the Airflow scheduler only ever posts to already-vetted URLs; the scheduler is a separate service/package with its own aiohttp client, outside the web app the report describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate public webhooks must keep working: custom user headers (e.g. Authorization) still sent, explicit non-default ports kept in Host, relative/public redirects followed up to 3 hops, Slack hooks.slack.com URLs accepted, and DEBUG mode still accepting http scheme; an over-broad fix (blocking all redirects, stripping headers, rejecting hostnames that need DNS, https-only) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: hostname 'localhost' incl. trailing dot and upper case
public hostname resolving to private IP, incl. mixed DNS answers
DNS rebinding between check and connect (pinned resolution)
redirect (absolute and relative Location) to an internal target
non-http schemes (file, gopher, ftp), userinfo credentials, invalid ports

O7_producer.where: Stored notification configuration JSON (web/projects/models.py:88) is written by views at web/projects/views.py:643 and :720 and read raw by the scheduler at scheduler/dags/includes/tasks/automations/actions.py:200-235; this is a persistence boundary, not a producer the check fails to call.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Scheduled webhook delivery: WebhookNotifier.send POSTs the stored extras.url via aiohttp with no destination validation, default redirect following and fresh DNS, and the response headers/body are persisted and shown in the automation execution drawer.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Form validation at save time already rejects internal URLs, so the scheduler 'only sees vetted URLs'; it is a separate Airflow service. Misses pre-fix rows, redirects and DNS rebinding.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Different top-level package (scheduler/dags/includes vs web/projects), different HTTP client (aiohttp vs urllib/requests), reached via automations actions.py

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Scheduled Slack delivery: SlackNotifier.send POSTs the stored extras.webhook_url via the same unvalidated aiohttp session; per-message response bodies are stored in execution details.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as webhook: URL already validated by SlackForm; Slack URLs are 'always hooks.slack.com'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: scheduler/dags/includes/notifiers.py, same file as the webhook route; falls together with it

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Save/reload boundary: notification rows saved before the form check existed (or written outside the forms) keep internal URLs and are dispatched by the scheduler without revalidation.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Data migration / legacy rows are an operational concern, not a code path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An automation action type that posts to a URL entered directly in the AutomationForm (e.g. 'call_webhook') without reusing _validate_notification_outbound_url.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Automations already carry typed actions with values (scheduler/dags/includes/tasks/automations/actions.py:188); a per-automation URL action is a natural feature a maintainer would add on a separate form.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Onboarding step that creates a webhook/Slack Notification via Notification.objects.create with a URL from the onboarding form, bypassing WebhookForm/SlackForm.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Onboarding already creates an email Notification directly from its own form; adding a Slack option there is a plausible product change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Django admin registration for Notification whose ModelAdmin edits configuration JSON directly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The latest commit added admin support for Automation in the same file; doing the same for Notification is the obvious next step.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918): user-controlled outbound webhook URL reaching loopback/private/metadata targets, with response reflected to the user
